meta.title: Governance Levels — Understanding the Foundation
meta.description: Learn what governance levels are, why they matter, and how to configure them for your organisation.

hero.title: What Are Governance Levels?
hero.subtitle: The constitutional backbone of your organisation's hierarchy
hero.summary: Governance levels define the chain of command in your organisation — from the global executive down to the local branch. Each level represents a tier in the hierarchy with its own committee, geographic scope, and authority.

points.title: Establish Clear Hierarchy
points.description: Define who reports to whom. Each level has a clear position in the organisational structure.

points.title: Enable Authority Delegation
points.description: Higher levels can delegate authority to lower levels while maintaining oversight.

points.title: Define Geographic Scope
points.description: Each level operates within a defined geographic area — global, continental, national, regional, or local.

points.title: Power Approval Workflows
points.description: Decisions flow through the hierarchy — lower levels propose, higher levels approve.

points.title: Tenant-Specific Configuration
points.description: Every organisation defines its own levels. Your hierarchy is independent from others.

fields.description: Numeric position in the hierarchy. Level 0 is the highest (global), higher numbers are more local.
What this level's committee is called, e.g. "Central Working Committee" or "District Executive".
A short identifier used in APIs and references, e.g. "CWC" or "DISTRICT_EXEC".
The geographic scope this level covers, e.g. "Nepal" or "Europe".
A short code for the geographic area, e.g. "NP" or "EU".
The parent geographic scope. Level 0 has no parent; each lower level references the level above it.
Uncheck to temporarily disable a level without deleting its configuration.
